paper_title: Searching for solar axions using data from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
notes: Paper constrains isovector axion-nucleon coupling |g3_aN| ≡ (1/2)|g_an - g_ap| > 2×10^-5 GeV^-1 at 95% CL for sub-MeV axion masses (up to ~5.5 MeV). The coupling is reported in GeV^-1 units in the paper. The exclusion is mass-independent (flat) across the stated validity range. The paper emphasizes this is a model-independent constraint on the isovector component. In the absence of precise cancellation between g_an and g_ap, this also constrains g_an individually. The detection mechanism is axion-induced deuteron dissociation (a + d → n + p) via solar axions produced in the p + d → 3He + a nuclear transition. Coupling type is AxionNeutron because the constraint is on nucleon couplings (specifically the isovector combination), and the paper does not distinguish between neutron and proton couplings in the primary result—it constrains their difference. However, the pre-analysis hint and the paper's focus on nucleon interactions (not specifically photon or electron) support AxionNeutron as the primary coupling type.
